saturation.note: The two treated arms saturated two windows each on FOUR DISJOINT calls, so the covariate is balanced in count and carried by different calls in each arm. A saturated window contributes the empty string to its arm's stitched hypothesis (reproduction.obs_loop's own quarantine), so it is charged no operation at all and its reference words fall out of that arm's totals as deletions charged to the neighbouring window's cursor. The sensitivity excludes the UNION from all three arms and is reported beside the primary, never in place of it. Two exclusions are reported, because the window-level one is nearly vacuous: a saturated window is charged NO reference word (it stitched nothing), so its untranscribed reference mass has already landed on the NEIGHBOURING window's deletion cursor and dropping the window cannot remove it. The CALL-level exclusion drops the whole cluster the saturated slice sits in, from all three arms, and is the one that actually bounds the covariate.

kc-e1.rule: reproduction.obs_loop: a slice whose completion reaches the decode cap is a TRUNCATED decode, not a transcript end, so it contributes the empty string to the stitched hypothesis and is counted instead of scored silently (obs_saturated true, obs_accepted_chars 0)
kc-e1.what_it_costs_the_measurement: 2 of 1,593 windows -- 180 s of 141,345.85, or 0.127 % of the audio -- carry no transcript, which lands in this cell's deletions and is one of the reasons its corpus WER moved. Both windows ran far past the typical ~1,550-char window (5,426 and 4,195 raw chars) before the cap stopped them, so the finding is over-generation under the brief, not a lost window at random. Reported, never repaired: the sealed hypothesis is what the OBS rule produced.
